pages.lesson:
LESSON: EXCLAMATORY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1.2: Exclamatory

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Exclamatory
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: When do you use an exclamatory or an imperative sentence in school?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify instances where the two types of sentences are used correctly in printed handouts or online texts
2. punctuate given texts by use of the appropriate punctuation marks
3. appreciate the use of exclamatory and imperative sentences in spoken language

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Exclamatory

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Exclamatory

Teach
• Focus skill: identify instances where the two types of sentences are used correctly in printed handouts or online texts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Exclamatory.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Exclamatory
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When do you use an exclamatory or an imperative sentence in school?
2. How do you decide whether to use an exclamation mark or a period at the end of a sentence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
